newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas holds near highs ahead of close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas holds near highs ahead of close.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still trading near session highs on Thursday shortly before the close after breaking through resistance earlier, industry sources said.

At 1430 EST, December was 13 cents higher at $2.775 per million British thermal units after the break through $2.75 led to additional technical buying and reports concerning a Gulf pipeline problem surfaced. January similarly rose 12.5 cents to $2.775.
"They're covering stops, and cash is still strong," said one futures trading, noting next resistance was now at $2.80.
Further resistance in December, which expires next Thursday, was seen at the $2.88 contract high, traders said.
Support in December was first pegged at $2.615, then the $2.53 area.
Fueling the early rally were market rumors that a pipeline problem may have disrupted service.
However, Tenneco Inc said this afternoon there were no natural gas disruptions to customers despite a minor problem on its BlueWater System.
A tracking device known as a pig became stuck in the offshore Louisiana system, but the company said it anticipated rectifying the problem within the next couple of hours.
At 1400 EST, NYMEX said 32,469 Henry Hub contracts had traded.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast prices rose by about one to three cents to the low-to-mid $2.70s, while Midcontinent prices eased into the mid-to-high $2.50s ahead of more seasonable weather this weekend.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas continued its rally to reach a high of $1.65, up 14 cents, triggered by much stronger cash prices at the AECO storage hub.
Sources reported closing deals for Friday gas flow at AECO in the low-C$2 per gigajoule area as cold temperatures were expected to linger through at least this weekend.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded for the sixth consecutive day. December stood at $2.45 but was bid at $2.50 and $2.53 late.
Permian cash prices held relatively steady in the low-$2.50s.
On the KCBT, December traded 10 cents higher to $2.57, while deferreds were steady to up 10 cents. The December East/West spread widened by three cents to 20.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
Cash prices at Waha were in line with futures in the mid-to-high $2.50s.
